## 1. Spec

Turn the intent into `spec.md`, the design an engineer builds from. No
code. Start from how the system works today (`docs/architecture.md` and the
code) and describe the change against it: the new and changed rules; the
API changes, with request and response examples and every new error; how
the server enforces the rules without keeping state; the page (what shows
when, keyboard and screen-reader use, small screens); which modules change
and how; what must keep working exactly as before; and how each line of the
intent's "How we will know it worked" and "What must not change" will be
checked. End with **Open questions**: each one gets the decision you took,
so nothing blocks the next phase.

## 2. Plan

Turn `spec.md` into `plan.md`, an implementation plan. No code. The first
line is `# Plan: <title>`. Then 2 to 4 phases, each a heading
`## Phase N: <name>` followed only by task lines `- [ ] <task>`, 3 to 6
tasks each. Each phase ends with a task that verifies it by running
something, and leaves the game working. Verification uses what every
session has: `python3` (the tests, a throwaway script, a server started
with `--port 0` and driven with `urllib`) and `ruff`. No browser and no
other tools: how the page looks and feels is checked by a person at the
preview after phase 3, so list those checks under a final heading
`## For the preview` as plain bullets, not boxes. Writing new tests is
phase 4 of this process, not part of this plan, but the existing tests
must keep passing after every phase.

## 3. Implement

Implement the first phase of `plan.md` that still has unchecked boxes, and
only that phase. Tick each box (`- [ ]` to `- [x]`) as soon as its task is
done, one edit per task. Follow `spec.md`. If you must depart from it,
update `spec.md` so the two agree. Keep `docs/architecture.md` true. Do not
write new tests yet, but run the existing ones. If a verify task asks for
something you cannot run, do the part you can, tick it, and add what is
left to `## For the preview`.

## Preview (done by a person)

A person runs the change on a preview server, goes through
`## For the preview`, and records the result in `preview.md`: who, when,
and what passed or failed. That file is the sign-off for everything only a
browser can show. Later phases read it; they do not repeat those checks.

## 4. Unit tests

Write pytest tests in `tests/` for every rule in `spec.md`, next to the
existing ones: every new rule, every new error, and every "must not change"
promise of the intent. Call the code directly, not over the network. Run
the whole suite. If a test finds a bug, fix the code and say so in your
final message.

## 5. System test

Test the real system from the outside, extending `tests/system/`: start
`python3 -m tictactoe --port 0` as a process and, over HTTP, play the new
feature end to end, including the attempts the intent says must fail, and
show that the old game still behaves as before. Always stop the server,
even when a test fails. Run the whole suite. Write `test-report.md`: what
was tested, the result, and any bugs found and fixed.

## 6. Lint

Run `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .`. Fix every finding in the
code, run the tests again, and stop when both are clean and the tests pass.
Never silence a finding (see `CLAUDE.md`).

## 7. Code review

Act as a reviewer who did not write this change. Read the intent, the spec,
the diff of the change (`git diff` against the commit before its spec) and
the code around it. Look for: bugs; gaps between intent, spec, code and
`docs/architecture.md`; rules that are not tested; security (the server
faces the internet and trusts no request); and accessibility. The browser
checks belong to `preview.md`: a problem it reports is a finding, but how
much a sign-off is worth (who looked, how closely) is for whoever releases
to judge, so say it in the verdict, not as a finding. Do not change any
code. Write `review.md`: one line per finding,

```markdown
- [ ] **blocker|major|minor** `path:line`: what is wrong, and why it matters
```

most severe first, then a one-paragraph verdict. If there is nothing to
report at some severity, say so; do not invent findings.

## 8. Review fixes

Fix every blocker and major finding in `review.md`, and the minors that
are cheap. Tick each finding as you fix it. Leave a finding you decide not
to fix unticked, with the reason after it. Add a test for every bug you
fix. Finish with the tests and lint clean.

## 9. Deploy

Follow `docs/deploy.md`.

# Intent: a secret cheat code

*From: Product. For: the games team. Change name: `cheat-code`.*

## Why

Tic-tac-toe has been live for a month. People play, but Hard can never be
beaten, and many players quit after two or three draws. Players love
secrets they can share with friends: we want a hidden cheat code that lets
you beat the computer once in a while. Players will pass the code around,
which brings them back to the page and brings their friends.

## What we want

- A secret code typed on the keyboard during a game against the computer
  unlocks a cheat for that game: the player may **steal** one square from
  the computer. The computer's mark on that square becomes the player's
  mark, and that counts as the player's move.
- One steal per game. It is never shown or hinted at on the page until the
  code has been typed. After that, the page makes clear how to use it.
- The code is the classic one: up, up, down, down, left, right, left, right,
  B, A.
- A game won with a steal is announced differently ("You won... with a
  little help"), and it is counted separately in the score. It must not
  count as a normal win.
- The cheat works only against the computer, at both levels, and not when
  two friends play on the same screen.

## What must not change

- Without the code, the game behaves exactly as it does today, and Hard
  still never loses to fair play.
- On the page, nobody can steal without typing the code. Nobody can steal
  twice in a game, even by sending requests to the server by hand.

## How we will know it worked

- It is live in production, the old game unchanged.
- People share the code: we see steals in games we did not set up ourselves.

  steal button, no hint, no "With help" column, and no change to labels or
  status texts. A screen reader announces nothing new.

  does nothing.
- Typing ↑ ↑ ↓ ↓ ← → ← → B A during a game against the computer (Easy and
  Hard) unlocks the steal: the panel and the "With help" column appear, and
  "Cheat unlocked! …" is announced.
- Typing it with uppercase B A works. Extra keys before the code still
  work, for example ↑ ↑ ↑ ↓ ↓ …. A wrong key in the middle does not unlock.

  and never plays a move. Typing it with the focus on a `<select>` does not

  turns it into an X, and the computer replies.

  focus to the lowest stealable O. The arrow keys move the focus, Enter
  steals, and Esc (or pressing the button again) cancels and puts the focus

  R, column C.").
- A win that used a steal shows "You won... with a little help". "With
  help" goes up by 1 and "X wins" does not. A computer win or a draw after a
  steal counts as today.
- A new game, a mode change or a level change hides the steal again until

- At 320 px wide, in light and dark mode, the panel and the four-column

  wrong: the game token does not match this game", and New game plays
  normally again.

The server side is sound and matches the spec. Every steal is judged on
the server. The HMAC game token binds the board, the level and the steal
count, is compared with `compare_digest`, and is handed out only on a chain
that starts from an empty board, so a second steal, a forged or edited
token, a hand-made board and friend-mode steals are all refused. The key is
never logged or sent. Requests without `game` and `steal` go through exactly
the old code path, Hard is unchanged for `steals=0`, and the unit and system
tests cover every rule, error and "must not change" promise in the spec
(including a 2318-request comparison with the baseline server). The page
works out no rule. None of the findings blocks a release.

Whoever releases must weigh one thing: **nobody has looked at the page.**
`preview.md` records an unattended run, "Checked by: nobody", "Result: not
checked", and the test report wrongly claims otherwise. So none of the
browser behaviour has been seen by a person: that the page is unchanged
before the code is typed, how the code is recognised, steal mode with mouse
and keyboard, the screen-reader announcements, the "With help" column, and
the 320 px layout. The 320 px fit depends on the CSS `:has()` selector, which
older browsers ignore. These parts of the intent's "must not change" promise
("the game behaves exactly as it does today", "nobody can steal without typing
the code" on the page) rest only on reading `app.js`.
# Spec: a secret cheat code (`cheat-code`)

Source: `changes/cheat-code/intent.md`. This is the design to build from.
It describes the change against the system as it is today
(`docs/architecture.md`, `tictactoe/`).

## Summary

Against the computer, typing ↑ ↑ ↓ ↓ ← → ← → B A on the page unlocks a
**steal** for the current game: once per game the player may turn one of
the computer's O squares into an X, and that is the player's move. A win
that used a steal is announced as "You won... with a little help" and
counted in its own score column, never as a normal win.

The browser recognises the code and shows the steal controls. The server
judges every steal. To enforce "one steal per game" without keeping state,
the server signs each game position it hands out (an HMAC **game token**)
and accepts a steal only together with a valid token that says no steal has
been used. Requests without a token behave exactly as today.

## How it works today (the parts this change touches)

- A board is 9 cells, `"X"`, `"O"` or `""`. Whose turn it is follows from
  the counts: `game.turn()` is X when X count == O count. `game.validate()`
  accepts a board only if X count − O count is 0 or 1.
- `POST /api/move` takes the whole board, `cell`, `mode`, `level`. Against
  the computer the player is X and the board must have X to move. The server
  plays `cell`, then the computer's reply, and answers the new board.
- The server trusts nothing: any board that passes `validate()` is accepted.
  It has no idea whether that board came from a real game.
- The score (X wins, O wins, draws) lives in `app.js` until reload.

## New and changed rules

1. **Steal.** In a game against the computer, on the player's turn (X to
   move, game still playing), the player may name one cell that holds `"O"`.
   That cell becomes `"X"`. This is the player's move: the computer then
   replies as usual if the game goes on.
2. **Once per game.** A game has at most one steal. A game is one unbroken
   chain of positions handed out by the server, starting from the empty
   board (see "Game token").
3. **Only against the computer**, at both levels (`easy`, `hard`). Never in
   `friend` mode.
4. **Turn after a steal.** A steal changes a mark without adding one, so the
   counts no longer say whose turn it is. The rule becomes: with `s` steals
   used in the game (0 or 1), X is to move when X count − O count == `s`,
   otherwise O. A valid board has X count − O count equal to `s` or `s + 1`.
   With `s = 0` both rules are exactly today's.
5. **A steal can win at once.** If the stolen square completes a line of X,
   the game is won by X and the computer does not move. A steal never fills
   an empty square, so it cannot cause a draw by itself.
6. **Assisted win.** A game won by X in which a steal was used is an
   *assisted* win. The server says so in every answer (`assisted: true`).
   The page announces it as "You won... with a little help"

1	"""HTTP server: the page, its assets, and the JSON move API.
     2	
     3	The server keeps no state between requests. The browser sends the whole
     4	board with every move, the server checks it, plays the move (and the
     5	computer's reply) and sends back the new board and where the game stands.
     6	"""
     7	
     8	import json
     9	from http import HTTPStatus
    10	from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
    11	from pathlib import Path
    12	
    13	from . import ai, game, signing
    14	
    15	STATIC = Path(__file__).parent / "static"
    16	# Only these files are served: a fixed map, so no path from a request ever
    17	# reaches the file system.
    18	ASSETS = {
    19	    "/": ("index.html", "text/html; charset=utf-8"),
    20	    "/static/style.css": ("style.css", "text/css; charset=utf-8"),
    21	    "/static/app.js": ("app.js", "text/javascript; charset=utf-8"),
    22	}
    23	MODES = ("computer", "friend")
    24	MAX_BODY = 1024
    25	
    26	
    27	def handle_move(request: object) -> dict:
    28	    """Answer one POST /api/move body. Raises IllegalMoveError on bad input."""
    29	    if not isinstance(request, dict):
    30	        raise game.IllegalMoveError("the body must be a JSON object")
    31	    # A field sent as null counts as not sent.
    32	    token = request.get("game")
    33	    stolen = request.get("steal")
    34	    # Without a token or a steal, exactly today's checks in today's order.
    35	    judged = token is not None or stolen is not None
    36	    if judged:
    37	        board = game.check_cells(request.get("board"))
    38	    else:
    39	        board = game.validate(request.get("board"))
    40	    mode = request.get("mode", "computer")
    41	    if mode not in MODES:
    42	        raise game.IllegalMoveError(f"mode must be one of: {', '.join(MODES)}")
    43	    level = request.get("level", "hard")
    44	    if mode == "computer":
    45	        if level not in ai.LEVELS:
    46	            raise game.IllegalMoveError(f"level must be one of: {', '.join(ai.LEVELS)}")
    47	        if not judged and game.turn(board) != "X":
    48	            raise game.IllegalMoveError("against the computer you play X")
    49	    steals = signing.verify(token, board, level) if token is not None else 0
    50	    if judged:
    51	        board = check_steal_request(request, board, mode, steals)
    52	    # A token proves a chain of positions from an empty board: hand out a
    53	    # first one only when this request starts a new game.
    54	    chained = token is not None or not any(board)
    55	    if stolen is not None:
    56	        board = game.steal(board, stolen, steals)
    57	        steals = 1
    58	    else:
    59	        board = game.play(board, request.get("cell"), steals)
    60	    computer_move = None
    61	    if mode == "computer" and game.outcome(board).status == "playing":
    62	        computer_move = ai.choose_move(board, level, steals=steals)
    63	        board = game.play(board, computer_move, steals)
    64	    answer = describe(board, steals) | {"computer_move": computer_move}
    65	    new_token = None
    66	    if mode == "computer" and answer["status"] == "playing" and chained:
    67	        new_token = signing.sign(board, level, steals)
    68	    can_steal = new_token is not None and steals == 0 and answer["turn"] == "X"
    69	    return answer | {
    70	        "game": new_token,
    71	        "stealable": [i for i, cell in enumerate(board) if cell == "O"] if can_steal else [],
    72	        "steal_used": steals == 1,
    73	        "assisted": answer["winner"] == "X" and steals == 1,
    74	    }
    75	
    76	
    77	def check_steal_request(request: dict, board: list[str], mode: str, steals: int) -> list[str]:
    78	    """The checks for a request with a token or a steal, after the token's."""
    79	    stolen = request.get("steal")
    80	    if stolen is not None:
    81	        if request.get("cell") is not None:
    82	            raise game.IllegalMoveError("send either cell or steal, not both")
    83	        if mode == "friend":
    84	            raise game.IllegalMoveError("you can only steal from the computer")
    85	        if request.get("game") is None:
    86	            raise game.IllegalMoveError("a steal needs the game token from the last answer")
    87	    board = game.validate(board, steals)
    88	    if mode == "computer" and game.turn(board, steals) != "X":
    89	        raise game.IllegalMoveError("against the computer you play X")
    90	    return board
    91	
    92	
    93	def describe(board: list[str], steals: int = 0) -> dict:
    94	    result = game.outcome(board)
    95	    return {
    96	        "board": board,
    97	        "status": result.status,
    98	        "winner": result.winner,
    99	        "line": list(result.line) if result.line else None,
   100	        "turn": game.turn(board, steals) if result.status == "playing" else None,
   101	    }
   102	
   103	
   104	class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
   105	    server_version = "tictactoe"
   106	
   107	    def do_GET(self) -> None:
   108	        self.serve(head=False)
   109	
   110	    def do_HEAD(self) -> None:
   111	        self.serve(head=True)
   112	
   113	    def do_POST(self) -> None:
   114	        if self.path != "/api/move":
   115	            self.reply_json(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND, {"error": "not found"})
   116	            return
   117	        length = self.headers.get("Content-Length", "")
   118	        if not length.isdigit():
   119	            self.reply_json(HTTPStatus.LENGTH_REQUIRED, {"error": "Content-Length required"})
   120	            return
   121	        if int(length) > MAX_BODY:
   122	            self.reply_json(HTTPStatus.REQUEST_ENTITY_TOO_LARGE, {"error": "body too large"})
   123	            return
   124	        try:
   125	            request = json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(length)) or b"null")
   126	            answer = handle_move(request)
   127	        except (ValueError, game.IllegalMoveError) as error:
   128	            # json.JSONDecodeError and IllegalMoveError are both ValueErrors
   129	            self.reply_json(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, {"error": str(error)})
   130	            return
   131	        self.reply_json(HTTPStatus.OK, answer)
   132	        if request.get("steal") is not None:
   133	            # Only a steal that was played gets here, so level and cell are
   134	            # known-good values. Never log the token, the key or the board.
   135	            self.log_message(
   136	                "steal level=%s cell=%d status=%s assisted=%s",
   137	                request.get("level", "hard"),
   138	                request["steal"],
   139	                answer["status"],
   140	                "true" if answer["assisted"] else "false",
   141	            )
   142	
   143	    def serve(self, *, head: bool) -> None:
   144	        path = self.path.split("?", 1)[0]
   145	        if path == "/health":
   146	            self.reply(HTTPStatus.OK, b"ok", "text/plain; charset=utf-8", head=head)
   147	        elif path in ASSETS:
   148	            name, content_type = ASSETS[path]
   149	            self.reply(HTTPStatus.OK, (STATIC / name).read_bytes(), content_type, head=head)
   150	        elif path == "/api/move":
   151	            self.send_response(HTTPStatus.METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED)
   152	            self.send_header("Allow", "POST")
   153	            self.send_header("Content-Length", "0")
   154	            self.end_headers()
   155	        else:
   156	            self.reply(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND, b"not found", "text/plain; charset=utf-8", head=head)
   157	
   158	    def reply_json(self, status: HTTPStatus, body: dict) -> None:
   159	        self.reply(status, json.dumps(body).encode(), "application/json")
   160	
   161	    def reply(
   162	        self, status: HTTPStatus, body: bytes, content_type: str, *, head: bool = False
   163	    ) -> None:
   164	        self.send_response(status)
   165	        self.send_header("Content-Type", content_type)
   166	        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
   167	        self.send_header("Cache-Control", "no-cache")
   168	        self.send_header("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff")
   169	        self.end_headers()
   170	        if not head:
   171	            self.wfile.write(body)
   172	
   173	
   174	def make_server(host: str, port: int) -> ThreadingHTTPServer:
   175	    return ThreadingHTTPServer((host, port), Handler)

    20	    "/static/style.css": ("style.css", "text/css; charset=utf-8"),
    21	    "/static/app.js": ("app.js", "text/javascript; charset=utf-8"),
    22	}
    23	MODES = ("computer", "friend")
    24	MAX_BODY = 1024
    25	
    26	
    27	def handle_move(request: object) -> dict:
    28	    """Answer one POST /api/move body. Raises IllegalMoveError on bad input."""
    29	    if not isinstance(request, dict):
    30	        raise game.IllegalMoveError("the body must be a JSON object")
    31	    # A field sent as null counts as not sent.
    32	    token = request.get("game")
    33	    stolen = request.get("steal")
    34	    # Without a token or a steal, exactly today's checks in today's order.
    35	    judged = token is not None or stolen is not None
    36	    if judged:
    37	        board = game.check_cells(request.get("board"))
    38	    else:
    39	        board = game.validate(request.get("board"))
    40	    mode = request.get("mode", "computer")
    41	    if mode not in MODES:
    42	        raise game.IllegalMoveError(f"mode must be one of: {', '.join(MODES)}")
    43	    level = request.get("level", "hard")
    44	    if mode == "computer":
    45	        if level not in ai.LEVELS:
    46	            raise game.IllegalMoveError(f"level must be one of: {', '.join(ai.LEVELS)}")
    47	        if not judged and game.turn(board) != "X":
    48	            raise game.IllegalMoveError("against the computer you play X")
    49	    steals = signing.verify(token, board, level) if token is not None else 0
    50	    if judged:
    51	        board = check_steal_request(request, board, mode, steals)
    52	    # A token proves a chain of positions from an empty board: hand out a
    53	    # first one only when this request starts a new game.
    54	    chained = token is not None or not any(board)
    55	    if stolen is not None:
    56	        board = game.steal(board, stolen, steals)
    57	        steals = 1
    58	    else:
    59	        board = game.play(board, request.get("cell"), steals)
    60	    computer_move = None
    61	    if mode == "computer" and game.outcome(board).status == "playing":
    62	        computer_move = ai.choose_move(board, level, steals=steals)
    63	        board = game.play(board, computer_move, steals)
    64	    answer = describe(board, steals) | {"computer_move": computer_move}
    65	    new_token = None
    66	    if mode == "computer" and answer["status"] == "playing" and chained:
    67	        new_token = signing.sign(board, level, steals)
    68	    can_steal = new_token is not None and steals == 0 and answer["turn"] == "X"
    69	    return answer | {
    70	        "game": new_token,
    71	        "stealable": [i for i, cell in enumerate(board) if cell == "O"] if can_steal else [],
    72	        "steal_used": steals == 1,
    73	        "assisted": answer["winner"] == "X" and steals == 1,
    74	    }
    75	
    76	
    77	def check_steal_request(request: dict, board: list[str], mode: str, steals: int) -> list[str]:
    78	    """The checks for a request with a token or a steal, after the token's."""
    79	    stolen = request.get("steal")
    80	    if stolen is not None:
    81	        if request.get("cell") is not None:
    82	            raise game.IllegalMoveError("send either cell or steal, not both")
    83	        if mode == "friend":
    84	            raise game.IllegalMoveError("you can only steal from the computer")
    85	        if request.get("game") is None:
    86	            raise game.IllegalMoveError("a steal needs the game token from the last answer")
    87	    board = game.validate(board, steals)
    88	    if mode == "computer" and game.turn(board, steals) != "X":
    89	        raise game.IllegalMoveError("against the computer you play X")
    90	    return board
    91	
    92	
    93	def describe(board: list[str], steals: int = 0) -> dict:
    94	    result = game.outcome(board)
    95	    return {
    96	        "board": board,
    97	        "status": result.status,
    98	        "winner": result.winner,
    99	        "line": list(result.line) if result.line else None,
   100	        "turn": game.turn(board, steals) if result.status == "playing" else None,
   101	    }
   102	
   103	
   104	class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
   105	    server_version = "tictactoe"
   106	
   107	    def do_GET(self) -> None:
   108	        self.serve(head=False)
   109	
   110	    def do_HEAD(self) -> None:
   111	        self.serve(head=True)
   112	
   113	    def do_POST(self) -> None:
   114	        if self.path != "/api/move":
   115	            self.reply_json(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND, {"error": "not found"})
   116	            return
   117	        length = self.headers.get("Content-Length", "")
   118	        if not length.isdigit():
   119	            self.reply_json(HTTPStatus.LENGTH_REQUIRED, {"error": "Content-Length required"})
   120	            return
   121	        if int(length) > MAX_BODY:
   122	            self.reply_json(HTTPStatus.REQUEST_ENTITY_TOO_LARGE, {"error": "body too large"})
   123	            return
   124	        try:
   125	            request = json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(length)) or b"null")
   126	            answer = handle_move(request)
   127	        except (ValueError, game.IllegalMoveError) as error:
   128	            # json.JSONDecodeError and IllegalMoveError are both ValueErrors
   129	            self.reply_json(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, {"error": str(error)})
   130	            return
   131	        self.reply_json(HTTPStatus.OK, answer)
   132	        if request.get("steal") is not None:
   133	            # Only a steal that was played gets here, so level and cell are
   134	            # known-good values. Never log the token, the key or the board.
   135	            self.log_message(
   136	                "steal level=%s cell=%d status=%s assisted=%s",
   137	                request.get("level", "hard"),
   138	                request["steal"],
   139	                answer["status"],
   140	                "true" if answer["assisted"] else "false",
   141	            )
   142	
   143	    def serve(self, *, head: bool) -> None:
   144	        path = self.path.split("?", 1)[0]
   145	        if path == "/health":
   146	            self.reply(HTTPStatus.OK, b"ok", "text/plain; charset=utf-8", head=head)
   147	        elif path in ASSETS:
   148	            name, content_type = ASSETS[path]
   149	            self.reply(HTTPStatus.OK, (STATIC / name).read_bytes(), content_type, head=head)
   150	        elif path == "/api/move":
   151	            self.send_response(HTTPStatus.METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED)
   152	            self.send_header("Allow", "POST")
   153	            self.send_header("Content-Length", "0")
   154	            self.end_headers()
   155	        else:
   156	            self.reply(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND, b"not found", "text/plain; charset=utf-8", head=head)
   157	
   158	    def reply_json(self, status: HTTPStatus, body: dict) -> None:
   159	        self.reply(status, json.dumps(body).encode(), "application/json")
   160	
   161	    def reply(
   162	        self, status: HTTPStatus, body: bytes, content_type: str, *, head: bool = False
   163	    ) -> None:
   164	        self.send_response(status)
   165	        self.send_header("Content-Type", content_type)
   166	        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
   167	        self.send_header("Cache-Control", "no-cache")
   168	        self.send_header("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff")
   169	        self.end_headers()
   170	        if not head:
   171	            self.wfile.write(body)
   172

   174	def make_server(host: str, port: int) -> ThreadingHTTPServer:
   175	    return ThreadingHTTPServer((host, port), Handler)

import pytest

from tictactoe import game, server, signing

EMPTY = [""] * 9


def test_a_move_against_the_computer_gets_a_reply() -> None:
    answer = server.handle_move({"board": EMPTY, "cell": 0, "mode": "computer", "level": "hard"})
    assert answer["board"][0] == "X"
    assert answer["computer_move"] is not None
    assert answer["board"][answer["computer_move"]] == "O"
    assert (answer["status"], answer["turn"]) == ("playing", "X")


def test_a_move_against_a_friend_does_not() -> None:
    answer = server.handle_move({"board": EMPTY, "cell": 4, "mode": "friend"})
    assert answer["board"] == ["", "", "", "", "X", "", "", "", ""]
    assert (answer["computer_move"], answer["turn"]) == (None, "O")


def test_a_winning_move_reports_the_line() -> None:
    cells = ["X", "X", "", "O", "O", "", "", "", ""]
    answer = server.handle_move({"board": cells, "cell": 2, "mode": "computer"})
    assert answer["status"] == "won"
    assert (answer["winner"], answer["line"]) == ("X", [0, 1, 2])
    assert (answer["turn"], answer["computer_move"]) == (None, None)


def test_the_computer_can_win() -> None:
    cells = ["O", "O", "", "X", "", "", "X", "", ""]
    answer = server.handle_move({"board": cells, "cell": 8, "mode": "computer", "level": "hard"})
    assert (answer["status"], answer["winner"], answer["computer_move"]) == ("won", "O", 2)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("request_body", "message"),
    [
        ([], "JSON object"),
        ({"cell": 0}, "board"),
        ({"board": EMPTY, "cell": 0, "mode": "online"}, "mode"),
        ({"board": EMPTY, "cell": 0, "level": "impossible"}, "level"),
        ({"board": ["X", *[""] * 8], "cell": 1, "mode": "computer"}, "you play X"),
        ({"board": EMPTY, "cell": 9}, "cell"),
    ],
)
def test_bad_requests_are_rejected(request_body: object, message: str) -> None:
    with pytest.raises(game.IllegalMoveError, match=message):
        server.handle_move(request_body)


# The cheat code's steal (changes/cheat-code/spec.md)

NEW_FIELDS = {"game", "stealable", "steal_used", "assisted"}
OLD_FIELDS = {"board", "status", "winner", "line", "turn", "computer_move"}
MISMATCH = "the game token does not match this game"


def board(text: str) -> list[str]:
    """A board from 9 characters, row by row: "X", "O" or "." for empty."""
    return ["" if c == "." else c for c in text.replace(" ", "")]


def move(cells: list[str], level: str = "hard", **fields: object) -> dict:
    return server.handle_move({"board": cells, "mode": "computer", "level": level, **fields})


def the_spec_game() -> dict:
    """The spec's example up to X's choice: X 0, O 4, X 8, O 1, with a token."""
    first = move(EMPTY, cell=0)
    return move(first["board"], cell=8, game=first["game"])


def test_the_first_move_of_a_new_game_gets_a_token() -> None:
    answer = move(EMPTY, cell=0)
    assert answer["board"] == board("X.. .O. ...")
    assert answer["game"].startswith("0.")
    assert (answer["stealable"], answer["steal_used"], answer["assisted"]) == ([4], False, False)


def test_sending_the_token_back_chains_the_game() -> None:
    answer = the_spec_game()
    assert answer["board"] == board("XO. .O. ..X")
    assert answer["game"].startswith("0.")
    assert answer["stealable"] == [1, 4]


def test_a_steal_that_wins_ends_the_game_assisted() -> None:
    before = the_spec_game()
    answer = move(before["board"], steal=4, game=before["game"])
    assert answer == {
        "board": board("XO. .X. ..X"),
        "status": "won",
        "winner": "X",
        "line": [0, 4, 8],
        "turn": None,
        "computer_move": None,
        "game": None,
        "stealable": [],
        "steal_used": True,
        "assisted": True,
    }


def test_a_steal_that_does_not_win_gets_the_computers_reply() -> None:
    before = the_spec_game()
    answer = move(before["board"], steal=1, game=before["game"])
    assert answer["board"] == board("XXO .O. ..X")
    assert (answer["status"], answer["turn"], answer["computer_move"]) == ("playing", "X", 2)
    assert answer["game"].startswith("1.")
    assert (answer["stealable"], answer["steal_used"], answer["assisted"]) == ([], True, False)


def test_a_second_steal_is_refused() -> None:
    before = the_spec_game()
    after = move(before["board"], steal=1, game=before["game"])
    with pytest.raises(game.IllegalMoveError, match="already stolen"):
        move(after["board"], steal=4, game=after["game"])


def test_the_game_goes_on_after_a_steal_and_stays_stolen() -> None:
    before = the_spec_game()
    after = move(before["board"], steal=1, game=before["game"])
    nxt = move(after["board"], cell=3, game=after["game"])
    assert nxt["board"][3] == "X"
    assert nxt["game"] is None or nxt["game"].startswith("1.")
    assert (nxt["stealable"], nxt["steal_used"]) == ([], True)
    if nxt["status"] == "playing":
        with pytest.raises(game.IllegalMoveError, match="already stolen"):
            move(nxt["board"], steal=nxt["board"].index("O"), game=nxt["game"])


def test_the_board_after_a_steal_needs_its_token() -> None:
    before = the_spec_game()

    # without the token, X one ahead on X's turn is today's error
    with pytest.raises(game.IllegalMoveError, match="you play X"):

    # an s = 0 token cannot be made for it without the key
    zero = "0" + after["game"][1:]
    with pytest.raises(game.IllegalMoveError, match=MISMATCH):

def test_every_steal_path_against_hard_has_at_most_one_steal() -> None:
    # Walk every game a player can play against Hard through the API, trying
    # every move and every steal, and check the rules on every answer.
    todo = [(EMPTY, None, False)]
    finished = 0
    while todo:
        cells, token, stolen = todo.pop()
        options = [{"cell": c} for c in game.legal_moves(cells)]

        for option in options:

            if "steal" in option and stolen:

            todo.append((answer["board"], answer["game"], used))
    assert finished > 100

    # Walk every game a player can play against Hard through the API, trying
    # every move and every steal, and check the rules on every answer.
    todo = [(EMPTY, None, False)]
    finished = 0
    while todo:
        cells, token, stolen = todo.pop()
        options = [{"cell": c} for c in game.legal_moves(cells)]
        options += [{"steal": c} for c in range(9) if cells[c] == "O"]
        for option in options:
            fields = {"game": token} if token else {}
            if "steal" in option and stolen:
                with pytest.raises(game.IllegalMoveError, match="already stolen"):
                    move(cells, **option, **fields)
                continue
            answer = move(cells, **option, **fields)
            used = stolen or "steal" in option
            assert answer["steal_used"] is used
            assert answer["assisted"] is (used and answer["winner"] == "X")
            if answer["status"] != "playing":
                assert (answer["game"], answer["stealable"]) == (None, [])
                finished += 1
                continue
            assert answer["game"].startswith("1." if used else "0.")
            o_cells = [i for i, c in enumerate(answer["board"]) if c == "O"]
            assert answer["stealable"] == ([] if used else o_cells)
            todo.append((answer["board"], answer["game"], used))
    assert finished > 100

def test_a_move_against_the_computer_gets_a_reply() -> None:
    answer = server.handle_move({"board": EMPTY, "cell": 0, "mode": "computer", "level": "hard"})
    assert answer["board"][0] == "X"
    assert answer["computer_move"] is not None
    assert answer["board"][answer["computer_move"]] == "O"
    assert (answer["status"], answer["turn"]) == ("playing", "X")


def test_a_move_against_a_friend_does_not() -> None:
    answer = server.handle_move({"board": EMPTY, "cell": 4, "mode": "friend"})
    assert answer["board"] == ["", "", "", "", "X", "", "", "", ""]
    assert (answer["computer_move"], answer["turn"]) == (None, "O")


def test_a_winning_move_reports_the_line() -> None:
    cells = ["X", "X", "", "O", "O", "", "", "", ""]
    answer = server.handle_move({"board": cells, "cell": 2, "mode": "computer"})
    assert answer["status"] == "won"
    assert (answer["winner"], answer["line"]) == ("X", [0, 1, 2])
    assert (answer["turn"], answer["computer_move"]) == (None, None)


def test_the_computer_can_win() -> None:
    cells = ["O", "O", "", "X", "", "", "X", "", ""]
    answer = server.handle_move({"board": cells, "cell": 8, "mode": "computer", "level": "hard"})
    assert (answer["status"], answer["winner"], answer["computer_move"]) == ("won", "O", 2)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("request_body", "message"),
    [
        ([], "JSON object"),
        ({"cell": 0}, "board"),
        ({"board": EMPTY, "cell": 0, "mode": "online"}, "mode"),
        ({"board": EMPTY, "cell": 0, "level": "impossible"}, "level"),
        ({"board": ["X", *[""] * 8], "cell": 1, "mode": "computer"}, "you play X"),
        ({"board": EMPTY, "cell": 9}, "cell"),
    ],
)
def test_bad_requests_are_rejected(request_body: object, message: str) -> None:
    with pytest.raises(game.IllegalMoveError, match=message):
        server.handle_move(request_body)


# The cheat code's steal (changes/cheat-code/spec.md)

NEW_FIELDS = {"game", "stealable", "steal_used", "assisted"}
OLD_FIELDS = {"board", "status", "winner", "line", "turn", "computer_move"}
MISMATCH = "the game token does not match this game"


def board(text: str) -> list[str]:
    """A board from 9 characters, row by row: "X", "O" or "." for empty."""
    return ["" if c == "." else c for c in text.replace(" ", "")]


def move(cells: list[str], level: str = "hard", **fields: object) -> dict:
    return server.handle_move({"board": cells, "mode": "computer", "level": level, **fields})


def the_spec_game() -> dict:
    """The spec's example up to X's choice: X 0, O 4, X 8, O 1, with a token."""
    first = move(EMPTY, cell=0)
    return move(first["board"], cell=8, game=first["game"])


def test_the_first_move_of_a_new_game_gets_a_token() -> None:
    answer = move(EMPTY, cell=0)
    assert answer["board"] == board("X.. .O. ...")
    assert answer["game"].startswith("0.")
    assert (answer["stealable"], answer["steal_used"], answer["assisted"]) == ([4], False, False)


def test_sending_the_token_back_chains_the_game() -> None:
    answer = the_spec_game()
    assert answer["board"] == board("XO. .O. ..X")
    assert answer["game"].startswith("0.")
    assert answer["stealable"] == [1, 4]


def test_a_steal_that_wins_ends_the_game_assisted() -> None:
    before = the_spec_game()
    answer = move(before["board"], steal=4, game=before["game"])
    assert answer == {
        "board": board("XO. .X. ..X"),
        "status": "won",
        "winner": "X",
        "line": [0, 4, 8],
        "turn": None,
        "computer_move": None,
        "game": None,
        "stealable": [],
        "steal_used": True,
        "assisted": True,
    }


def test_a_steal_that_does_not_win_gets_the_computers_reply() -> None:
    before = the_spec_game()
    answer = move(before["board"], steal=1, game=before["game"])
    assert answer["board"] == board("XXO .O. ..X")
    assert (answer["status"], answer["turn"], answer["computer_move"]) == ("playing", "X", 2)
    assert answer["game"].startswith("1.")
    assert (answer["stealable"], answer["steal_used"], answer["assisted"]) == ([], True, False)


def test_a_second_steal_is_refused() -> None:
    before = the_spec_game()
    after = move(before["board"], steal=1, game=before["game"])
    with pytest.raises(game.IllegalMoveError, match="already stolen"):
        move(after["board"], steal=4, game=after["game"])


def test_the_game_goes_on_after_a_steal_and_stays_stolen() -> None:
    before = the_spec_game()
    after = move(before["board"], steal=1, game=before["game"])
    nxt = move(after["board"], cell=3, game=after["game"])
    assert nxt["board"][3] == "X"
    assert nxt["game"] is None or nxt["game"].startswith("1.")
    assert (nxt["stealable"], nxt["steal_used"]) == ([], True)
    if nxt["status"] == "playing":
        with pytest.raises(game.IllegalMoveError, match="already stolen"):
            move(nxt["board"], steal=nxt["board"].index("O"), game=nxt["game"])


def test_the_board_after_a_steal_needs_its_token() -> None:
    before = the_spec_game()
    after = move(before["board"], steal=1, game=before["game"])
    # without the token, X one ahead on X's turn is today's error
    with pytest.raises(game.IllegalMoveError, match="you play X"):
        move(after["board"], cell=3)
    # an s = 0 token cannot be made for it without the key
    zero = "0" + after["game"][1:]
    with pytest.raises(game.IllegalMoveError, match=MISMATCH):
        move(after["board"], steal=4, game=zero)


def test_a_steal_works_at_easy() -> None:
    first = move(EMPTY, "easy", cell=0)
    o_cell = first["board"].index("O")
    answer = move(first["board"], "easy", steal=o_cell, game=first["game"])
    assert answer["board"][o_cell] == "X"
    assert answer["steal_used"] is True
    assert answer["game"] is None or answer["game"].startswith("1.")


def test_a_later_win_after_a_steal_is_assisted() -> None:
    cells = board("XX. OO. X..")
    answer = move(cells, cell=2, game=signing.sign(cells, "hard", 1))
    assert (answer["status"], answer["winner"]) == ("won", "X")
    assert (answer["assisted"], answer["steal_used"], answer["game"]) == (True, True, None)


def test_a_win_without_a_steal_is_not_assisted() -> None:
    cells = board("XX. OO. ...")
    answer = move(cells, cell=2, game=signing.sign(cells, "hard", 0))
    assert (answer["status"], answer["winner"]) == ("won", "X")
    assert (answer["assisted"], answer["steal_used"]) == (False, False)


def test_a_computer_win_after_a_steal_is_a_normal_o_win() -> None:
    cells = board("X.. OO. XX.")
    answer = move(cells, cell=1, game=signing.sign(cells, "hard", 1))
    assert (answer["status"], answer["winner"], answer["computer_move"]) == ("won", "O", 5)
    assert (answer["assisted"], answer["steal_used"], answer["game"]) == (False, True, None)


def test_a_draw_after_a_steal_is_a_normal_draw() -> None:
    cells = board("XOX XO. OX.")
    answer = move(cells, cell=8, game=signing.sign(cells, "hard", 1))
    assert (answer["status"], answer["computer_move"]) == ("draw", 5)
    assert (answer["assisted"], answer["steal_used"], answer["game"]) == (False, True, None)


def test_every_steal_path_against_hard_has_at_most_one_steal() -> None:
    # Walk every game a player can play against Hard through the API, trying
    # every move and every steal, and check the rules on every answer.
    todo = [(EMPTY, None, False)]
    finished = 0
    while todo:
        cells, token, stolen = todo.pop()
        options = [{"cell": c} for c in game.legal_moves(cells)]
        options += [{"steal": c} for c in range(9) if cells[c] == "O"]
        for option in options:
            fields = {"game": token} if token else {}
            if "steal" in option and stolen:
                with pytest.raises(game.IllegalMoveError, match="already stolen"):
                    move(cells, **option, **fields)
                continue
            answer = move(cells, **option, **fields)
            used = stolen or "steal" in option
            assert answer["steal_used"] is used
            assert answer["assisted"] is (used and answer["winner"] == "X")
            if answer["status"] != "playing":
                assert (answer["game"], answer["stealable"]) == (None, [])
                finished += 1
                continue
            assert answer["game"].startswith("1." if used else "0.")
            o_cells = [i for i, c in enumerate(answer["board"]) if c == "O"]
            assert answer["stealable"] == ([] if used else o_cells)
            todo.append((answer["board"], answer["game"], used))
    assert finished > 100


def test_replaying_an_older_token_branches_the_game() -> None:
    # Open questions 3: accepted, and the branch still has one steal at most
    first = move(EMPTY, cell=0)
    second = move(first["board"], cell=8, game=first["game"])
    move(second["board"], steal=1, game=second["game"])
    branch = move(first["board"], steal=4, game=first["game"])
    assert branch["steal_used"] is True
    if branch["status"] == "playing":
        with pytest.raises(game.IllegalMoveError, match="already stolen"):
            move(branch["board"], steal=branch["board"].index("O"), game=branch["game"])


def test_a_hand_made_board_without_a_token_cannot_steal() -> None:
    cells = board("XO. ... ...")
    answer = move(cells, cell=8)
    assert (answer["game"], answer["stealable"], answer["steal_used"]) == (None, [], False)
    with pytest.raises(game.IllegalMoveError, match="needs the game token"):
        move(answer["board"], steal=1)


def test_a_friend_game_gets_the_new_fields_and_never_a_token() -> None:
    answer = server.handle_move({"board": EMPTY, "cell": 4, "mode": "friend"})
    assert {k: answer[k] for k in NEW_FIELDS} == {
        "game": None,
        "stealable": [],
        "steal_used": False,
        "assisted": False,
    }


def test_no_steal_against_a_friend() -> None:
    request = {"board": board("XO. ... ..."), "steal": 1, "mode": "friend"}
    with pytest.raises(game.IllegalMoveError, match="only steal from the computer"):
        server.handle_move(request)


FRIEND_TOKEN = "the game token is only for games against the computer"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("cells", "steals", "fields"),
    [
        # review finding: a computer game's after-steal token used to be
        # honoured in friend mode, and the answer said steal_used: true
        ("XXO .O. ..X", 1, {"cell": 3}),
        ("XO. ... ...", 0, {"cell": 2}),
        ("XO. ... ...", 0, {"steal": 1}),
        ("XO. ... ...", None, {"cell": 2, "game": "bad"}),
    ],
)
def test_a_friend_game_refuses_a_token(cells: str, steals: int | None, fields: dict) -> None:
    grid = board(cells)
    if steals is not None:
        fields = {**fields, "game": signing.sign(grid, "hard", steals)}
    request = {"board": grid, "mode": "friend", **fields}
    with pytest.raises(game.IllegalMoveError, match=f"^{FRIEND_TOKEN}$"):
        server.handle_move(request)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "request_body",
    [
        {"board": EMPTY, "cell": 0, "mode": "computer", "level": "hard"},
        {"board": board("XO. ... ..."), "cell": 8, "mode": "computer"},
        {"board": board("XX. OO. ..."), "cell": 2},
        {"board": EMPTY, "cell": 4, "mode": "friend"},
        {"board": board("X.. ... ..."), "cell": 4, "mode": "friend"},
    ],
)
def test_without_a_token_only_the_four_fields_are_added(request_body: dict) -> None:
    answer = server.handle_move(request_body)
    assert set(answer) == OLD_FIELDS | NEW_FIELDS
    # a field sent as null counts as not sent
    assert server.handle_move({**request_body, "game": None, "steal": None}) == answer


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("request_body", "message"),
    [
        ({"board": EMPTY, "cell": 0, "game": None, "steal": None, "mode": "x"}, "mode"),
        ({"board": board("X.. ... ..."), "cell": 1, "game": None}, "you play X"),
        ({"board": board("XX. ... ..."), "cell": 1, "steal": None}, "alternate"),
        ({"board": EMPTY, "cell": 9, "game": None}, "cell"),

def test_every_request_with_a_token_is_checked() -> None:
    cells = board("XO. ... ...")
    token = signing.sign(cells, "hard", 0)
    with pytest.raises(game.IllegalMoveError, match=MISMATCH):
        move(board("XO. ... ..X"), cell=7, game=token)
    with pytest.raises(game.IllegalMoveError, match=MISMATCH):
        move(cells, "easy", cell=4, game=token)
    with pytest.raises(game.IllegalMoveError, match=MISMATCH):
        move(cells, cell=4, game="")
    with pytest.raises(game.IllegalMoveError, match=MISMATCH):
        move(cells, cell=4, game=["0", token[2:]])
    assert move(cells, cell=4, game=token)["game"].startswith("0.")


def test_a_hand_edited_board_breaks_the_token() -> None:
    before = the_spec_game()
    edited = list(before["board"])
    edited[1] = ""
    with pytest.raises(game.IllegalMoveError, match=MISMATCH):
        move(edited, steal=4, game=before["game"])

        # each error of the spec's table
        ("XO. ... ...", 0, {"cell": 2, "steal": 1}, "send either cell or steal, not both"),
        ("XO. ... ...", None, {"steal": 1}, "a steal needs the game token from the last answer"),

def test_steal_errors(cells: str, steals: int | None, fields: dict, message: str) -> None:

    if steals is not None:
        fields = {**fields, "game": signing.sign(grid, "hard", steals)}

"""The cheat code's steal, played over HTTP against the real server.

The server runs with a known TICTACTOE_SECRET, as production does, and its
log is kept so the tests can read what it prints.
"""

from collections.abc import Iterator
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from .client import post, serve

SECRET = "system-test-secret-0123456789abcdef"
EMPTY = [""] * 9
NEW_FIELDS = ("game", "stealable", "steal_used", "assisted")


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def server(tmp_path_factory: pytest.TempPathFactory) -> Iterator[tuple[str, Path]]:
    log = tmp_path_factory.mktemp("server") / "server.log"
    with log.open("w") as stream, serve(secret=SECRET, log=stream) as base:
        yield base, log


@pytest.fixture
def url(server: tuple[str, Path]) -> str:
    return server[0]


def move(url: str, **body: object) -> dict:
    """A move that must succeed; returns the answer."""
    code, answer = post(f"{url}/api/move", body)
    assert code == 200, answer
    return answer


def refused(url: str, **body: object) -> str:
    """A move that must be refused with 400; returns the error message."""
    code, answer = post(f"{url}/api/move", body)
    assert code == 400, answer
    return answer["error"]


def hard_opening(url: str) -> dict:
    """X 0, O 4, X 8, O 1 against Hard: stealing 4 wins, stealing 1 does not."""
    first = move(url, board=EMPTY, cell=0, level="hard")
    answer = move(url, board=first["board"], cell=8, level="hard", game=first["game"])
    assert answer["board"] == ["X", "O", "", "", "O", "", "", "", "X"]
    assert answer["stealable"] == [1, 4]
    return answer


# --- The steal, end to end ---------------------------------------------------


def test_the_first_move_of_a_game_gets_a_token(url: str) -> None:
    answer = move(url, board=EMPTY, cell=0, level="hard")
    assert answer["game"].startswith("0.")
    assert answer["board"][answer["computer_move"]] == "O"
    assert answer["stealable"] == [answer["computer_move"]]
    assert (answer["steal_used"], answer["assisted"]) == (False, False)


def test_a_steal_that_wins_at_once_is_an_assisted_win(url: str) -> None:
    before = hard_opening(url)
    answer = move(url, board=before["board"], steal=4, level="hard", game=before["game"])
    assert answer == {
        "board": ["X", "O", "", "", "X", "", "", "", "X"],
        "status": "won",
        "winner": "X",
        "line": [0, 4, 8],
        "turn": None,
        "computer_move": None,
        "game": None,
        "stealable": [],
        "steal_used": True,
        "assisted": True,
    }


def test_a_steal_is_the_players_move_and_the_computer_replies(url: str) -> None:
    before = hard_opening(url)
    answer = move(url, board=before["board"], steal=1, level="hard", game=before["game"])
    assert answer["board"] == ["X", "X", "O", "", "O", "", "", "", "X"]
    assert answer["computer_move"] == 2
    assert (answer["status"], answer["turn"]) == ("playing", "X")
    assert answer["game"].startswith("1.")
    assert answer["stealable"] == []
    assert (answer["steal_used"], answer["assisted"]) == (True, False)


def test_after_a_steal_the_game_plays_on_to_its_end(url: str) -> None:
    before = hard_opening(url)
    answer = move(url, board=before["board"], steal=1, level="hard", game=before["game"])
    while answer["status"] == "playing":
        assert answer["steal_used"] is True
        assert answer["stealable"] == []
        assert answer["game"].startswith("1.")
        cell = answer["board"].index("")
        answer = move(url, board=answer["board"], cell=cell, level="hard", game=answer["game"])
    assert answer["game"] is None
    assert answer["steal_used"] is True
    assert answer["assisted"] is (answer["winner"] == "X")


@pytest.mark.parametrize("seed_cell", [0, 4, 8])
def test_a_steal_works_at_easy(url: str, seed_cell: int) -> None:
    answer = move(url, board=EMPTY, cell=seed_cell, level="easy")
    assert answer["stealable"]
    target = answer["stealable"][0]
    after = move(url, board=answer["board"], steal=target, level="easy", game=answer["game"])
    assert after["board"][target] == "X"
    assert after["steal_used"] is True
    if after["status"] == "playing":
        assert after["game"].startswith("1.")
        assert after["board"][after["computer_move"]] == "O"
    assert after["assisted"] is (after["winner"] == "X")


def test_the_stealable_squares_are_the_os_on_the_players_turn(url: str) -> None:
    answer = move(url, board=EMPTY, cell=0, level="hard")
    while answer["status"] == "playing":
        assert answer["stealable"] == [i for i, c in enumerate(answer["board"]) if c == "O"]
        cell = answer["board"].index("")
        answer = move(url, board=answer["board"], cell=cell, level="hard", game=answer["game"])
    assert answer["stealable"] == []
    assert answer["game"] is None

def test_the_token_is_bound_to_the_board(url: str) -> None:

    error = refused(url, board=other, steal=4, level="hard", game=before["game"])
    assert error == "the game token does not match this game"


def test_the_token_is_bound_to_the_level(url: str) -> None:
    before = hard_opening(url)
    error = refused(url, board=before["board"], steal=4, level="easy", game=before["game"])
    assert error == "the game token does not match this game"


def test_editing_the_steal_count_breaks_the_token(url: str) -> None:
    before = hard_opening(url)
    after = move(url, board=before["board"], steal=1, level="hard", game=before["game"])

    raised = "1" + before["game"][1:]
    error = refused(url, board=before["board"], cell=2, level="hard", game=raised)
    assert error == "the game token does not match this game"

    assert error == "the game token does not match this game"


def test_the_token_is_bound_to_the_level(url: str) -> None:
    before = hard_opening(url)
    error = refused(url, board=before["board"], steal=4, level="easy", game=before["game"])
    assert error == "the game token does not match this game"


def test_editing_the_steal_count_breaks_the_token(url: str) -> None:
    before = hard_opening(url)
    after = move(url, board=before["board"], steal=1, level="hard", game=before["game"])
    reset = "0" + after["game"][1:]
    error = refused(url, board=after["board"], steal=4, level="hard", game=reset)
    assert error == "the game token does not match this game"
    raised = "1" + before["game"][1:]
    error = refused(url, board=before["board"], cell=2, level="hard", game=raised)
    assert error == "the game token does not match this game"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(

1	# Architecture
2	
3	```text
4	browser (static/)                          server (Python, stdlib)
5	┌───────────────────────┐  POST /api/move  ┌────────────────────────────┐
6	│ index.html  app.js    │ ───────────────▶ │ server.py  handle_move()   │
7	│ draws, sends clicks,  │    whole board   │   ├─ game.py  rules        │
8	│ keeps the score       │ ◀─────────────── │   └─ ai.py    computer     │
9	└───────────────────────┘   new board +    └────────────────────────────┘
10	                            outcome
11	```
12	
13	The rules live in Python only. The browser never decides whether a move is
14	legal or who won: it shows what the server answers.
15	
16	## Modules (`tictactoe/`)
17	
18	| File | Job |
19	|------|-----|
20	| `game.py` | The rules. A board is a list of 9 cells, row by row, each `"X"`, `"O"` or `""`. X moves first, so `turn(board, steals=0)` follows from the counts: with `steals` steals used in the game (0 or 1), X is to move when X count − O count == `steals`. `check_cells(board)` checks only a board's shape and cells, `validate(board, steals=0)` checks a whole board from outside (`check_cells`, then X − O must be `steals` or `steals + 1`), `play(board, cell, steals=0)` returns a new board (never changes its input) or raises `IllegalMoveError`, `steal(board, cell, steals)` returns a new board with the O on `cell` turned into an X (once per game, on X's turn, only an O), `outcome()` says `playing`, `won` (with winner and line) or `draw`. With `steals=0` everything is the plain game. |
21	| `ai.py` | The computer. `choose_move(board, level, rng=None, *, steals=0)`: **hard** is negamax over the full game tree, cached (per board and `steals`), lowest cell among equals, so it is deterministic and never loses; **easy** takes a winning move if it sees one, otherwise plays at random. `steals` is passed on to every rule call, so the search knows whose turn it is after a steal. |
22	| `signing.py` | The game token. The key is `TICTACTOE_SECRET` when set and not empty, otherwise 32 random bytes made at start-up; it is the only module that reads `os.environ`, and the key never leaves it. `sign(board, level, steals)` returns `"<s>.<mac>"`, the HMAC-SHA256 (lowercase hex) of `tictactoe-game-v1|<level>|<s>|<cells>`, cells written `X`, `O` or `-`. `verify(token, board, level)` returns `s`, or raises `IllegalMoveError("the game token does not match this game")`; it compares with `hmac.compare_digest`. |
23	| `server.py` | `ThreadingHTTPServer`. Serves a fixed map of assets (no request path reaches the file system), `/health`, and the move API (`handle_move`, with `check_steal_request` for requests that carry a token or a steal). Keeps no state: what it must trust it signs with `signing.py`. Logs one line per successful steal. |
24	| `__main__.py` | `python3 -m tictactoe [--host] [--port]`; prints the URL it listens on. |
25	| `static/` | `index.html`, `style.css`, `app.js`. No build step, no libraries. |
26	
27	## The move API
28	
29	`POST /api/move`, a JSON body of at most 1024 bytes:
30	
31	```json
32	{"board": ["X", "", "", "", "O", "", "", "", ""], "cell": 2, "mode": "computer", "level": "hard",
33	 "game": "0.<64 hex>"}
34	```
35	
36	- `mode` is `computer` (default) or `friend`; `level` is `easy` or `hard`
37	  (default), used only against the computer.
38	- Against the computer the player is always X, so the board must have X
39	  to move.
40	- The server plays `cell` for whoever is to move, then, against the
41	  computer and if the game goes on, the computer's reply as O.
42	- `game` (optional) is the token from the previous answer. `steal`
43	  (optional, instead of `cell`) is a cell holding an O that the player
44	  turns into an X, as their move: once per game, only against the computer,
45	  and only together with a `game` token. A field sent as `null` counts as
46	  not sent.
47	
48	Answer `200`:
49	
50	```json
51	{"board": ["X", "", "X", "", "O", "", "", "", "O"], "status": "playing",
52	 "winner": null, "line": null, "turn": "X", "computer_move": 8,
53	 "game": "0.<64 hex>", "stealable": [4, 8], "steal_used": false, "assisted": false}
54	```
55	
56	`status` is `playing`, `won` or `draw`; `line` is the three winning cells;
57	`turn` is `null` once the game is over; `computer_move` is `null` when the
58	computer did not move. `game` is the token for the new position (below) or
59	`null`; `stealable` lists the O cells when the answer's token has `s = 0`,
60	the game is playing and X is to move, else `[]`; `steal_used` is `true`
61	once the game has used its steal; `assisted` is `true` for a win by X with
62	`steal_used`. The page uses these as given and works out none of them.
63	
64	### The game token, and why the server stays stateless
65	
66	To allow one steal per game without remembering games, the server signs
67	each position it hands out (`signing.py`): the token `"<s>.<mac>"` binds
68	the board, the level and `s`, the steals used so far. It is handed out
69	only in `computer` mode while the game is `playing`: with the request's
70	`s` (or `1` after a steal) when the request carried a valid token, with
71	`s = 0` when the request had no token and an empty board (a new game), and
72	otherwise `game` is `null` (a hand-made mid-game board plays as before but
73	can never steal). A steal needs an `s = 0` token; after it every token in
74	that game has `s = 1`, and forging one needs the key. An old token stays
75	valid, so a player can go back to an earlier position of the same game
76	and steal there: a branch, which still has at most one steal.
77	
78	**Turn after a steal.** A steal changes a mark without adding one, so with
79	`s` steals used X is to move when X − O == `s`, and a valid board has
80	X − O equal to `s` or `s + 1`. With `s = 0` this is the plain rule.
81	
82	**Without `game` and `steal`** a request goes through exactly the old
83	checks and gets the old answer, plus the four new fields.
84	
85	Errors: `400 {"error": "..."}` for any bad input (bad JSON, impossible
86	board, taken square, game over, unknown mode or level), `411` without a
87	`Content-Length`, `413` for a body over 1024 bytes, `404` for other paths,
88	`405` for `GET /api/move`. A request with `game` or `steal` is checked in
89	this order: the body, the board's shape and cells, mode, level; then
90	
91	| Case | Message |
92	|------|---------|
93	| `game` does not verify for this `board` and `level` | `the game token does not match this game` |
94	| both `cell` and `steal` | `send either cell or steal, not both` |
95	| `steal` in `friend` mode | `you can only steal from the computer` |
96	| `steal` without `game` | `a steal needs the game token from the last answer` |
97	| X − O outside `s`..`s + 1` | `X moves first and the players alternate` |
98	| not X to move under `s`, against the computer | `against the computer you play X` |
99	| `steal` with an `s = 1` token | `you have already stolen a square in this game` |
100	| `steal` not a whole number 0–8 | `steal must be a whole number from 0 to 8` |
101	| the game is over | `the game is over` |
102	| the cell is not an O | `you can only steal one of the computer's squares` |
103	
104	A normal move with a token then gets `play`'s usual errors.
105	
106	**Log.** After each successful steal the server writes one line through
107	`log_message` (stderr), `steal level=hard cell=4 status=won assisted=true`,
108	and nothing else: no token, no key, no board.
109	
110	## The page
111	
112	`app.js` holds the current answer from the server and the score (X wins, O
113	wins, draws, and wins with help, until the page is reloaded). Each click or Enter/Space on a
114	square sends one move. The board is one tab stop: arrow keys, Home and End
115	move between squares (roving `tabindex`), and every square has an
116	`aria-label` such as "Row 1, column 3, X, winning". The status line is an
117	`aria-live` region. Changing mode or level starts a new game.
118	
119	`app.js` keeps the whole last answer, including `game`, `stealable`,
120	`steal_used` and `assisted`; a new game starts with `game: null`. Every
121	move request sends the last answer's `game` token back, and leaves it out
122	while it is `null` (the first move of a game, friend mode, a game that has
123	ended). An error, such as "the game token does not match this game" after a
124	development restart, shows in the status line, and New game recovers.
125	
126	`index.html` also holds the cheat panel under the status line (`#cheat`: the
127	"Steal a square" button `#steal` with `aria-pressed`, and the text
128	`#cheat-text`) and a fourth score column "With help" (`#score-help-head`,
129	`#score-help`). All of them carry `hidden`, and `style.css` makes `hidden`
130	win over every display rule, so until the cheat is unlocked the page looks
131	and reads exactly as before. `style.css` styles them: a dashed frame on
132	`.cell.stealable` (shape, not colour alone), a steal button at least 44 px
133	tall, and tighter score cells once the fourth column shows, so it fits
134	320 px.
135	
136	### The cheat code
137	
138	- **Recognising it.** A `keydown` listener on `document` keeps the last 10
139	  keys and compares them with `ArrowUp ArrowUp ArrowDown ArrowDown ArrowLeft
140	  ArrowRight ArrowLeft ArrowRight b a` (B and A in either case), so extra
141	  keys before the code do not matter. It ignores keys with Ctrl, Alt or
142	  Meta, auto-repeat, and keys typed in a `<select>`. The board's own arrow
143	  handling is unchanged: typing the code on the board only moves the focus.
144	  The code is plain in `app.js`: it is shared on purpose.
145	- **Locking per game.** The code unlocks only in `computer` mode while the
146	  game is `playing`; otherwise it does nothing at all. New game, a mode
147	  change or a level change locks it again and clears the keys. The server
148	  does not know about the code; it only judges steals.
149	- **Unlocking** shows the panel and the "With help" column and announces
150	  "Cheat unlocked! Once this game, you may steal one of the computer's
151	  squares." in the status line. Such messages (`notice` in `app.js`) stay
152	  until the next answer from the server, then the usual text returns.
153	- **The panel.** The button is `aria-disabled="true"` (still focusable)
154	  while the answer's `stealable` is empty, and the text says why: "No O to
155	  steal yet", or "Steal used" once `steal_used`. Otherwise it says "Press
156	  Steal, then choose an O. Esc cancels."
157	- **Steal mode.** The button (click, Enter, Space) turns it on only when
158	  `stealable` is not empty: `aria-pressed="true"`, the status says "Steal:
159	  choose one of the computer's squares.", and the focus moves to the lowest
160	  stealable square (roving `tabindex`). Only the squares in `stealable` are
161	  then `aria-disabled="false"`, with class `stealable` and ", can be stolen"
162	  in their label; every other square does nothing. Choosing one sends
163	  `{board, steal, mode, level, game}`. Steal mode ends with the answer (or
164	  an error), or with Esc or a second press of the button, which puts the
165	  focus back on the button. Outside steal mode an O does nothing, as before.
166	- **After a steal.** While the game goes on, the status says "You stole row
167	  R, column C.". An answer with `assisted: true` shows "You won... with a
168	  little help" and adds 1 to "With help", not to "X wins"; O wins and draws
169	  count as before. The column stays visible until the page is reloaded.
170	  `app.js` uses `stealable`, `steal_used` and `assisted` as the server sends
171	  them and works out no rule.
172	
173	## Tests
174	
175	- `tests/test_game.py`, `tests/test_ai.py`, `tests/test_server.py`: unit
176	  tests. `test_hard_never_loses` plays Hard against every possible opponent,
177	  as X and as O.
178	- `tests/system/test_http.py`: starts `python3 -m tictactoe --port 0` as a
179	  process and tests it over HTTP: health, assets, 404s, whole games, errors.

```json
{"board": ["X", "", "", "", "O", "", "", "", ""], "cell": 2, "mode": "computer", "level": "hard",
 "game": "0.<64 hex>"}
```

- `mode` is `computer` (default) or `friend`; `level` is `easy` or `hard`
  (default), used only against the computer.
- Against the computer the player is always X, so the board must have X
  to move.
- The server plays `cell` for whoever is to move, then, against the
  computer and if the game goes on, the computer's reply as O.
- `game` (optional) is the token from the previous answer. `steal`
  (optional, instead of `cell`) is a cell holding an O that the player
  turns into an X, as their move: once per game, only against the computer,
  and only together with a `game` token. A field sent as `null` counts as
  not sent.

Answer `200`:

```json
{"board": ["X", "", "X", "", "O", "", "", "", "O"], "status": "playing",
 "winner": null, "line": null, "turn": "X", "computer_move": 8,
 "game": "0.<64 hex>", "stealable": [4, 8], "steal_used": false, "assisted": false}
```

`status` is `playing`, `won` or `draw`; `line` is the three winning cells;
`turn` is `null` once the game is over; `computer_move` is `null` when the
computer did not move. `game` is the token for the new position (below) or
`null`; `stealable` lists the O cells when the answer's token has `s = 0`,
the game is playing and X is to move, else `[]`; `steal_used` is `true`
once the game has used its steal; `assisted` is `true` for a win by X with
`steal_used`. The page uses these as given and works out none of them.

### The game token, and why the server stays stateless

To allow one steal per game without remembering games, the server signs
each position it hands out (`signing.py`): the token `"<s>.<mac>"` binds
the board, the level and `s`, the steals used so far. It is handed out
only in `computer` mode while the game is `playing`: with the request's
`s` (or `1` after a steal) when the request carried a valid token, with
`s = 0` when the request had no token and an empty board (a new game), and
otherwise `game` is `null` (a hand-made mid-game board plays as before but
can never steal). A steal needs an `s = 0` token; after it every token in
that game has `s = 1`, and forging one needs the key. An old token stays
valid, so a player can go back to an earlier position of the same game
and steal there: a branch, which still has at most one steal.

**Turn after a steal.** A steal changes a mark without adding one, so with
`s` steals used X is to move when X − O == `s`, and a valid board has
X − O equal to `s` or `s + 1`. With `s = 0` this is the plain rule.

**Without `game` and `steal`** a request goes through exactly the old
checks and gets the old answer, plus the four new fields.

Errors: `400 {"error": "..."}` for any bad input (bad JSON, impossible
board, taken square, game over, unknown mode or level), `411` without a
`Content-Length`, `413` for a body over 1024 bytes, `404` for other paths,
`405` for `GET /api/move`. A request with `game` or `steal` is checked in
this order: the body, the board's shape and cells, mode, level; then

| Case | Message |
|------|---------|
| `game` does not verify for this `board` and `level` | `the game token does not match this game` |
| both `cell` and `steal` | `send either cell or steal, not both` |
| `steal` in `friend` mode | `you can only steal from the computer` |
| `steal` without `game` | `a steal needs the game token from the last answer` |
| X − O outside `s`..`s + 1` | `X moves first and the players alternate` |
| not X to move under `s`, against the computer | `against the computer you play X` |
| `steal` with an `s = 1` token | `you have already stolen a square in this game` |
| `steal` not a whole number 0–8 | `steal must be a whole number from 0 to 8` |
| the game is over | `the game is over` |
| the cell is not an O | `you can only steal one of the computer's squares` |

A normal move with a token then gets `play`'s usual errors.

`log_message` (stderr), `steal level=hard cell=4 status=won assisted=true`,
and nothing else: no token, no key, no board.

## The page

`app.js` holds the current answer from the server and the score (X wins, O
wins, draws, and wins with help, until the page is reloaded). Each click or Enter/Space on a
square sends one move. The board is one tab stop: arrow keys, Home and End
move between squares (roving `tabindex`), and every square has an
`aria-label` such as "Row 1, column 3, X, winning". The status line is an

`app.js` keeps the whole last answer, including `game`, `stealable`,

and reads exactly as before. `style.css` styles them: a dashed frame on

tall, and tighter score cells once the fourth column shows, so it fits
320 px.

- **Recognising it.** A `keydown` listener on `document` keeps the last 10
  keys and compares them with `ArrowUp ArrowUp ArrowDown ArrowDown ArrowLeft
  ArrowRight ArrowLeft ArrowRight b a` (B and A in either case), so extra
  keys before the code do not matter. It ignores keys with Ctrl, Alt or

  handling is unchanged: typing the code on the board only moves the focus.

  game is `playing`; otherwise it does nothing at all. New game, a mode
  change or a level change locks it again and clears the keys. The server
  does not know about the code; it only judges steals.

  squares." in the status line. Such messages (`notice` in `app.js`) stay

  steal yet", or "Steal used" once `steal_used`. Otherwise it says "Press
  Steal, then choose an O. Esc cancels."

# Architecture

```text
browser (static/)                          server (Python, stdlib)
┌───────────────────────┐  POST /api/move  ┌────────────────────────────┐

│ draws, sends clicks,  │    whole board   │   ├─ game.py  rules        │
│ keeps the score       │ ◀─────────────── │   └─ ai.py    computer     │
└───────────────────────┘   new board +    └────────────────────────────┘
                            outcome
```

The rules live in Python only. The browser never decides whether a move is
legal or who won: it shows what the server answers.

## Modules (`tictactoe/`)

| File | Job |
|------|-----|
| `game.py` | The rules. A board is a list of 9 cells, row by row, each `"X"`, `"O"` or `""`. X moves first, so `turn(board, steals=0)` follows from the counts: with `steals` steals used in the game (0 or 1), X is to move when X count − O count == `steals`. `check_cells(board)` checks only a board's shape and cells, `validate(board, steals=0)` checks a whole board from outside (`check_cells`, then X − O must be `steals` or `steals + 1`), `play(board, cell, steals=0)` returns a new board (never changes its input) or raises `IllegalMoveError`, `steal(board, cell, steals)` returns a new board with the O on `cell` turned into an X (once per game, on X's turn, only an O), `outcome()` says `playing`, `won` (with winner and line) or `draw`. With `steals=0` everything is the plain game. |
| `ai.py` | The computer. `choose_move(board, level, rng=None, *, steals=0)`: **hard** is negamax over the full game tree, cached (per board and `steals`), lowest cell among equals, so it is deterministic and never loses; **easy** takes a winning move if it sees one, otherwise plays at random. `steals` is passed on to every rule call, so the search knows whose turn it is after a steal. |
| `signing.py` | The game token. The key is `TICTACTOE_SECRET` when set and not empty, otherwise 32 random bytes made at start-up; it is the only module that reads `os.environ`, and the key never leaves it. `sign(board, level, steals)` returns `"<s>.<mac>"`, the HMAC-SHA256 (lowercase hex) of `tictactoe-game-v1|<level>|<s>|<cells>`, cells written `X`, `O` or `-`. `verify(token, board, level)` returns `s`, or raises `IllegalMoveError("the game token does not match this game")`; it compares with `hmac.compare_digest`. |
| `server.py` | `ThreadingHTTPServer`. Serves a fixed map of assets (no request path reaches the file system), `/health`, and the move API (`handle_move`, with `check_steal_request` for requests that carry a token or a steal). Keeps no state: what it must trust it signs with `signing.py`. Logs one line per successful steal. |
| `__main__.py` | `python3 -m tictactoe [--host] [--port]`; prints the URL it listens on. |
